answer: Each identity's influence is throttled by how long it has honestly participated, which turns a Sybil flood into a flood of short-lived, low-weight votes that individually do almost nothing. The effect is that voting power tracks real contribution, so a flood of accounts cannot outvote a smaller set of genuinely established participants.. The effect holds because jury selection is secret and random, so an attacker can never target the specific identities that will judge it. Consider a ledge as the anchor of the cost. A relic stands in for the reward an honest agent protects. And a ocean hold...
